question: Assume today is 2026-09-12. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of passengers at London Heathrow Airport in September 2026, as reported in Heathrow's monthly traffic statistics.

target.what: Total passengers passing through London Heathrow Airport (LHR) during the calendar month of September 2026, as reported in Heathrow's monthly traffic statistics (terminal and transit passengers counted per airport traffic convention)
target.publisher: Heathrow Airport Limited (monthly traffic statistics / operational figures)
target.caveats: Period is future/ongoing relative to the 2026-09-12 cutoff, so no September 2026 actual exists; must be forecast. Definitional issues: Heathrow monthly figures typically count terminal passengers (excluding direct transit passengers) and may include or exclude transfers; domestic vs international sp

candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 passengers ≈ September 2025 actual scaled by recent year-on-year growth trend observed in months published before cutoff (Jan–Jul 2026). September is a peak summer-shoulder month with stable seasonal shape.
candidates.data_to_find: Heathrow monthly passenger totals for September 2023, September 2024, September 2025; and monthly totals Jan–Jul 2026 with YoY % changes. Minimum: Sept 2025 level plus latest 2026 YoY growth rate.
search_hints: Heathrow monthly traffic statistics 2025 passengers September
Heathrow traffic figures July 2026 year on year

candidates.hypothesis: Passengers = seat capacity offered at LHR in September 2026 × load factor × (1 − transit share). Schedule data (OAG/Cirium) gives seats; load factors ~80-85%; transit small.
candidates.data_to_find: LHR scheduled departing seat capacity for September 2026 (or Sept 2025 as proxy) from OAG/Cirium/airline schedule summaries; typical LHR load factor; transit passenger share. Substitute: annual seat capacity from ACL slot coordination reports.

candidates.hypothesis: Passengers ≈ daily passenger throughput × 30 days; throughput bounded by runway movement cap (~1,300 movements/day) × passengers per movement (~150-160). Gives an upper bound and central estimate.
candidates.data_to_find: Heathrow daily air transport movements (ATM) for September 2025/2026, passengers per ATM, and any operational cap. Minimum: annual ATM and annual passengers to derive passengers per movement.
search_hints: Heathrow runway movements per day cap

candidates.hypothesis: CAA publishes monthly terminal passenger totals for UK airports including Heathrow; September 2026 CAA data may lag but Sept 2025 and 2026 partials constrain the level and seasonality.
candidates.data_to_find: CAA monthly airport data for Heathrow: September 2024, September 2025 terminal passengers; 2026 monthly figures available before cutoff. Substitute: UK overall airport passenger trends.
search_hints: CAA airport statistics Heathrow monthly passengers

candidates.hypothesis: Heathrow or parent (FGP/ADR) guidance and analyst traffic forecasts for 2026 imply an annual passenger total; September share of annual (~8.5-9%) converts to monthly.
candidates.data_to_find: Heathrow 2026 annual passenger guidance/forecast; historical September share of annual passengers (2015-2025). Minimum: one annual forecast plus seasonal share.

candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 level may deviate from trend due to strikes, ATC disruptions, geopolitical events, or demand shocks between cutoff and month-end; these shift the estimate around the trend baseline.
candidates.data_to_find: Known scheduled strikes/disruptions at LHR for September 2026 announced before cutoff; any capacity cuts or route suspensions; comparison to prior disruption months' passenger impact.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
